newsitem.title: DUBAI: British-Dubai trade talks held on yacht Britannia.
newsitem.headline: British-Dubai trade talks held on yacht Britannia.

text.p: Trade officials from Britain and Dubai met on board the royal yacht Britannia on Saturday to discuss boosting bilateral business relations already valued at more than $1.6 billion last year.

Britain's junior Foreign Office minister Jeremy Hanley opened the inaugural session of the "United Kingdom-Dubai Trade and Economic Committee" aboard the luxury mini-liner, which is on its farewell foreign cruise before being decommissioned later this year.

The UAE's Minister of State for Finance and Industrial Affairs Ahmed bin Humaid al-Tayer headed the Dubai delegation at the meeting, held in the royal drawing room of the 44-year-old floating residence of the British monarchy.

"The purpose of the new committee is to identify new areas of cooperation and development of trade and partnerships and to remove barriers that exist to future trade," Hanley said, flanked by the pin-striped British delegation on one side and Dubai officials in gilded flowing robes on the other.

"In 1996, visible two-way trade topped one billion sterling ($1.62 billion) for the first time," he added. The figure did not include banking and service sector business which he estimated to be worth an additional one billion sterling.

Britain is one of the main trading partners of Dubai, the business centre of the UAE's seven emirates. Hanley said British exports to Dubai had risen by 16 percent in 1996 over 1995, while Dubai exports to Britain had jumped by 26 percent.
Britain and the UAE also signed a defence pact in November that British arms makers hope will pave the way for more business in the Gulf.
The committee was formed on the intitiative of Dubai. Tayer said the group would meet every six months.
"The formation of this high-level committee is an indication of the importance we all attach to its success," Tayer said.

Britain's trade with the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states -- the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain -- rose by more than 20 percent in the first 11 months of 1996 to 5.93 billion sterling on the same period in 1995.

Dubai was the first port of call on the Britannia's tour of the Gulf, part of its final, seven-month deployment which will culminate in its visit to Hong Kong in June for the handover ceremonies of the colony to China.
The ship, which arrived on Friday, was due to depart Dubai later on Saturday and continue to Qatar, Bahrain and Kuwait before leaving the Gulf for India and the Far East.
